about: Cases where the Rust engine deliberately differs from the recorded 3.6 behaviour. The oracle test fails if a case here stops differing, or differs in another way.

divergences.reason: strict-end: 3.6 accepted one trailing line break because the .NET '$' anchor matches before it. An identifier with a line break must not reach a command line.
strict-end: same as above, at the 200-character limit.
strict-end: 3.6 built a WinGet command line containing the line break.
strict-end: an exported identifier with a line break is rejected like any other invalid identifier.
strict-end: a saved selection cannot carry a key with a line break.
strict-end: 3.6 accepted a registry path ending in a line break as a cleanup candidate.

shared-folder-name: 3.6 took the name of the install folder of a verified app for a name of the product, whatever it was. An app installed into a folder that programs share then claimed the folders and registry keys of that name of every other program. The folder name now counts only when it shares the product name.
shared-folder-name: same as above, for an app whose ownership of the folder was verified.
shared-folder-name: same as above; the folder is called Other, which has nothing of the name Tool.
shared-folder-name: a registry key named like the install folder, and unlike the product, is no longer offered as a leftover.

shared-folder-name: a Windows trace of a program inside the install folder is offered only when that folder is named after the product; an app installed into a shared folder would otherwise claim the traces of every program in it.
